proof: Induct on the finite Littlestone dimension d. At the root of any shattered tree, the two restrictions have dimensions a,b at most d, and they cannot both equal d (otherwise their complete trees join to give dimension d+1). Thus a≤d and b≤d-1 after ordering. Induction bounds each subtree's randomized value by its Littlestone dimension, so the root tree has half its expected branch length at most 1/2+(a+b)/2≤d. Taking suprema proves the claim; the infinite case follows by truncation.
proof_source: The randomized-tree definition is Definition 1 of \cite{filmus2023randomized}; the comparison is a direct induction.
